clue.text: Carpeted under the table

definitions.meaning: to be carpeted is to be called in and severely reprimanded
someone under the table is helplessly drunk

explanation.surface: Someone was dressed down at work, then drank themselves to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: a severe telling-off, and a slang word for very drunk.

clue.text: Regularly visits relatives to support husband

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so it follows the other piece

parts.note: aunts are relatives

explanation.surface: A dutiful family member keeps calling round to help out a man of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt a place is to frequent it, going there habitually.

clue.text: Quiet after Greek character digs for fungi

indicators.note: says the quiet piece comes after the Greek letter

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sh is the call for quiet
digs are lodgings, rented rooms

explanation.surface: A silent Greek figure digs about in search of fungi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like a verb but is the noun for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are the familiar fruiting bodies of many fungi, an example of the class.

clue.text: Describe former lover? Unattractive

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
plain means homely, not good-looking

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to describe their old flame and answers bluntly: not attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to set it out clearly, to give an account of it.

clue.text: Leaves site to work around ten

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the ten
letters put to work are set going in a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A builder knocks off from the site around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' rearranges SITE into EITS, which goes 'around' X.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits as a verb means goes out or departs, just as leaves does.

clue.text: Busts — they slow you down, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is said aloud, and a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: brakes are the devices that slow a vehicle

explanation.surface: A wry remark that busts, whether arrests or breakdowns, put the brakes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bust something is to smash or wreck it, a synonym of breaking it.

clue.text: Indicates the Queen's pulled up trousers

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
cords are corduroy trousers

explanation.surface: A royal hitching up her trousers as a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns ER into RE; the 's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge records or indicates a reading, so the verbs are synonyms here.

clue.text: Greek somewhat ticklish? Somewhat

indicators.note: the closing Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Greek is a little ticklish, and getting a non-committal answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft pointed its indicator at the first 'somewhat', which is part of the hiding place; the closing 'Somewhat' is the hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes Attica and its Athenian dialect, so it is a word for Greek.

clue.text: Naughty nude lady's wanting adult at once

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and fall out of order
wanting means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A cheeky nude lady, with nothing grown-up about her, appears all of a sudden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes A from NUDELADYS; 'Naughty' rearranges the remaining NUDELDYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Suddenly and at once both mean immediately, without warning.

clue.text: Hair in two different directions — daughter's worried

indicators.note: the hair goes inside the two compass points

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are two compass points
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A daughter frets over her hair sticking out every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stressed is anxious and under strain, which is to say worried.

clue.text: Naive doctor enthusiastic about operation day

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the operation
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A wide-eyed doctor is overly keen about the day of surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' turns ENTHUSIASTIC into UNSHISTICATE, which goes 'about' OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated means lacking worldly experience, the same as naive.

clue.text: Dangers from cures limiting hospital

indicators.note: the cures piece surrounds and confines the hospital

parts.note: treats as a verb means cures or tends medically
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Risks that arise when remedies are kept out of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats are menaces or sources of possible harm, i.e. perils.

clue.text: Complaint made by artist embraced by every European

indicators.note: the artist sits inside the other letters

parts.note: each means every one
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a painter whom every European hugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and a sore ear is one.

clue.text: Associates Charlie with leg caught in fishing equipment

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
on is the cricket term for the leg side of the field

indicators.note: the caught letter goes inside the fishing gear

parts.note: nets are used for fishing
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Charlie and his gammy leg tangled up in the fishing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate two things is to link them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Move closer with Mercedes stuck in traffic

indicators.note: the car is wedged inside the other word

parts.note: to come is to approach, move closer
Merc is the short name for a Mercedes car

explanation.surface: Edging forward with a Mercedes jammed in the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like road congestion, but means trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in goods means dealing or trading, the same as commerce.

clue.text: Hold up pen

definitions.meaning: to hold up is to delay or play for time
a pen is an enclosure for livestock

explanation.surface: A robbery with a writing implement, or simply a brief instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to delay; the other is a compartment for an animal in a stable.

clue.text: Benefit expert at one's disposal

parts.note: avail as a noun means use or benefit
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: An offer of skilled help and its advantages, ready whenever needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available can be used when wanted, ready to hand.

clue.text: Many pull item out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, wrong

explanation.surface: A shopper hauls lots of things off the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiple means numerous, more than one, as many does.

clue.text: Unhappy at university clique

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
a set is a social circle or clique

explanation.surface: A student miserable about the in-crowd on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset as an adjective means distressed, sad.

clue.text: Steaming out of river's current

indicators.note: the river letter comes out of the steaming word

parts.note: tropical heat is steaming, hot and humid
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Steam rising off a river's flowing water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a flow of water but means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical concerns present-day matters, so it is current.

clue.text: Out of date medicine that is valued 50% off

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: half the word is knocked off, leaving the front half

explanation.surface: A sale on expired pills, now half price.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval is used loosely to mean hopelessly old-fashioned, antiquated.

clue.text: Volatile rodent found in Morecambe, perhaps

indicators.note: the rodent is placed inside the name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise; perhaps marks him as an example of an Eric
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A jumpy rat spotted in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morecambe' looks like the Lancashire resort, but is the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable, liable to sudden change, as volatile does.

clue.text: College cracked my clue

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast that a whole college solved the setter's clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum is a school or place of learning, after Aristotle's in Athens.

clue.text: Tramp stumbles around atomic base

indicators.note: the stumbling word goes around the atomic letter

parts.note: trips means stumbles
A stands for atomic, as in A-bomb
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A vagrant trips over at a nuclear installation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun but is the verb, to trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily, trudging, as to tramp does.

clue.text: Book ultimately missing conclusion

indicators.note: the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: at last means finally, ultimately

explanation.surface: A novel that turns out to have no ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound volume of maps, a kind of book.

clue.text: Honourably short time to recover

parts.note: mo is a moment, a short time
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: Behaving decently while recovering in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting morally means acting ethically, with honour.

clue.text: Ludicrously busy chap in charge

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man running things and absurdly overworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means frenzied and hyperactive, wildly busy.

clue.text: Open basic cell to criminal? One might

definitions.text: Open basic cell to criminal? One might

indicators.note: criminal letters are bent, rearranged from their lawful order

explanation.surface: Asking who would unlock a bare cell for a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: an officer is the one who opens a cell to a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer escorts arrested criminals and opens custody cells to lock them up.

clue.text: Simply starts to eat alternative snack items — like yoghurt

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice to eat different snacks, yoghurt for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily and simply both mean without difficulty.

clue.text: Dessert came with rice, strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A pudding served oddly alongside rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen sweet, a common example of a pudding course.
